clues: This city sits in the northeast of Thailand, on the north bank of a wide river. It is one of the four big cities of its region.
Winters stay dry and warm here, then hard rain comes with the monsoon from late April to October. Nights stay warm even when days turn a bit cool.
It was founded in the late 1700s by Thao Kham Phong. In 1792 it was made the main town of its large northeast region by the king.
During the Vietnam War, this city held a major United States air base. War planes flew from here for the Thai air force as well.
Each July, crowds watch a grand parade of huge carved beeswax art. The fair marks the start of the Buddhist rains retreat each year.
